t: Founded by the Kurdish commander Saladin, it united Egypt, Syria and Upper Mesopotamia against the Crusader states.
Saladin's victory at Hattin and recapture of Jerusalem in 1187 permanently shifted the balance in the Levant.
Divided among quarrelling kinsmen, it was overthrown by its own mamluk soldiers in 1250 and finished by the Mongols.
dyk: Saladin's nephew, Sultan al-Kamil, later handed Jerusalem to Emperor Frederick II by treaty in 1229, in return for help against his own Ayyubid relatives.
ev: Saladin ends the Fatimid Caliphate, restoring Egypt to Sunni Abbasid allegiance
After Nur al-Din's death, Saladin takes Damascus
Saladin destroys the Crusader army at Hattin and takes Jerusalem
Treaty of Jaffa ends the Third Crusade with Jerusalem still in Ayyubid hands
Saladin dies, triggering a succession struggle among his sons
Al-Kamil cedes Jerusalem to Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II
Bahri mamluks murder Sultan Turanshah and seize Egypt
Mongols invade the Levant, sack Aleppo and end Ayyubid rule in Syria
